open_points.subject: Registry endpoint validation at startup
open_points.text: R0-10 says the service is configured by environment variables “which it validates when it starts”; A6/A30 and this flow instead say “The Registry endpoint is not one of them: the service starts without it.”
open_points.question: Must a missing or unusable REGISTRY_BASE_URL prevent startup, or may startup succeed and only later Registry calls fail?
options: Validate REGISTRY_BASE_URL at startup and refuse to start
Start without REGISTRY_BASE_URL; fail each Registry call as transport_error
open_points.default_guess: Follow the more specific A6/A30 and State 4 flow: start successfully and fail only Registry calls.

witness.initial: REGISTRY_BASE_URL is absent when the deployment process starts the service.
outcomes: Startup is refused because every configuration environment variable must be validated at startup under R0-10.
Startup succeeds because the Registry endpoint is explicitly excluded from startup settings; a later Registry operation fails with transport_error.
witness.observer: The deployment process and health monitor see whether the service starts and answers health checks.

open_points.subject: Lifetime of binary-storage environment configuration
open_points.text: The flow says runtime_settings owns “reading the environment, once: the closed table config.runtime_environment_variables”; State 3 says binary_storage reads BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT and BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES “at each binary read.” BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES is also a required member of the startup configuration in A30.
open_points.question: Are BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT and BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES fixed in RuntimeSettings at startup, or re-read from the environment for every binary request?
options: Use the startup RuntimeSettings snapshot for every read
Re-read both variables for every binary read
Validate them at startup but also re-read them later
open_points.default_guess: Preserve the running-service exception stated in State 3: validate the startup value where required, then re-read the binary variables for each binary operation.

witness.initial: The service starts with BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES set to 1000 and passes all startup consistency checks.
events: An operator changes BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES to 2000 without restarting the service.
An authorized caller requests a 1500-byte binary.
outcomes: The request is refused because environment configuration was read once and the active bound remains 1000.
binary_storage accepts the read because it re-reads the environment and observes 2000.
witness.observer: The authorized binary caller sees either a refusal or the binary response.

open_points.subject: Readiness storage failure response
open_points.text: The flow says “readiness fails with the storage failure of module:portal_store” and constrains disclosure, but does not state the readiness HTTP status or whether the response is an empty error or a non-ok HealthStatus.
open_points.question: What exact HTTP outcome does readiness return when opening the database, creating a schema, or rolling back the readiness transaction fails?
options: HTTP 500 with an empty body under the general persistence error policy
open_points.default_guess: Return HTTP 500 with an empty body, applying the general persistence/storage failure translation.

witness.initial: The service is running, but its configured SQLite database cannot be opened.
events: module:runtime asks module:portal_store to begin the readiness transaction.
outcomes: The general failure policy is applied: HTTP 500 with an empty body.
Readiness-specific semantics are inferred: HTTP 503, possibly carrying a safe non-ok HealthStatus.
witness.observer: The monitor or deployment proxy sees a different status and possibly a different response body.
